name: Unidata
short: Egocentric and teleoperation robot data collected to order.

tasks: first-person video of household activities (coffee-making, cooking, object handling, chores)
RGB video with depth, full-body pose, hand pose, 6DoF head pose and synchronised IMU
teleoperation on the client's robot via VR controllers, space mice or exoskeleton rigs
kinesthetic demonstrations with joint states, end-effector pose and force-torque logged

pricing.notes: No price is published. 'we'll scope, price, and schedule' (egocentric page); for robotics, pricing is agreed at the 'Agreement & NDA' stage.

latency.typical: Most projects start delivering within two weeks
latency.notes: Stated on the egocentric page; the robotics page gives no turnaround.

freshness.typical_age: Captured after scoping and a sample or pilot
freshness.notes: A base dataset (4,050 hours, 15,000+ scenarios) is also licensed; that is archive, not a commission.

coverage.notes: No collection countries are listed. Contact address is Meydan Grandstand, Dubai, UAE.

licensing.summary: Egocentric page: 'Every participant signs a commercial-use release before recording' and the base dataset is 'available under a commercial license'. Robotics page: 'All data collected on your equipment belongs to you and stays under NDA.' The terms-of-use URL currently serves only a cookie policy, so no contractual ownership, AI-training or resale clause could be read. The privacy policy names consent as the basis for 'Training and/or testing of neural network algorithm models' using anonymised data, in a different context (anti-spoofing). AI training and resale of delivered data are not stated.

human.unknown: Participants sign a commercial-use release ('Mixed age and gender across hundreds of contributors'); a release is a rights document, not an identity check at enrolment (STANDARD §3). How collectors are recruited, identified or vetted is not published.

application.unknown: No capture-app or device attestation is documented.

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Wearable and tracking rigs: Pico 4 Ultra headsets, motion trackers, ZED stereo cameras, tactile gloves, grippers (robotics page). No C2PA or signed capture; Unidata is not on the C2PA conforming products list.

time.method: Streams are time-synchronised across modalities (IMU, depth, pose).
time.unknown: Synchronisation aligns streams to each other; no signed capture time.

content.method: A sample or pilot batch precedes the agreement, then 'Quality Control' (robotics page); a Quality Control Department page exists.
content.unknown: Acceptance criteria and QC results are not published.

corroboration.unknown: No independent check of collected data is documented.

auth.how_to_get: Contact via unidata.pro/contact-us (info@unidata.pro); steps: briefing and scope, sample or pilot, agreement and NDA.

mcp.notes: No server found in the official MCP Registry (searched the provider name, 2026-10-27).

api.notes: No API or ordering docs. No /.well-known/ucp, agent-card.json, irlpls or oauth-protected-resource document found (2026-10-27).

delivery.basis: 'Most projects start delivering within two weeks.' (a start, not completion)

payment.notes: No payment methods published; terms are agreed at the Agreement & NDA stage.

consent.method: 'Every participant signs a commercial-use release before recording.'
consent.unknown: The release text, bystander handling and withdrawal are not published.

requester.unknown: Unidata publishes no check of who commissions collection or for what; projects start with a briefing and an NDA.

summary: Unidata (Unidata L.L.C-FZ, Dubai) collects first-person video of daily activities with synchronised depth, pose and IMU, and teleoperation or kinesthetic demonstrations on the client's own robot. Scope, volume and price are agreed with the team; no price is published. It states that every participant signs a commercial-use release and that most projects start delivering within two weeks. Its terms page published today is only a cookie policy, so ownership and AI-training rights of delivered data are not stated beyond 'data collected on your equipment belongs to you'.
